summary: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and Heidelberg University. He taught at Fergusson College, served as Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1939–2001), and held professorial and dean roles at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Ramesh Chandra Negi works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as a research assistant (attested 2001–2004) and associate professor (attested 2026), teaching Ruth Gamble and Andy Rotman.

Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta, Presidency University, and other colleges. He held posts at the universities of Calcutta, Dhaka, Chicago, and Pennsylvania, served as principal at BHU, and presided over the Asiatic Society.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. In 1967, he served as department head at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and was a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest University, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State University.

Ramin Etesami is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at International Buddhist College, where he was supervised by Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina (attested 2015).
Ramkrishna Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Calcutta and held a post at Ananda Mohan College from circa 1974 to 2007.
Ramon Prats is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017).
Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied under teachers Steven D. Goodman and Richard Payne, who served as his doctoral supervisor.

Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist and sinologist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley under James Alan Matisoff. He served as professor at City University of Hong Kong (~1996–2006) and held a post at Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai (2021).

Rangama Chandawimala, a Buddhist studies scholar, earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha, and studied under Attaragama Gnanawimala. He is an associate professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught numerous students such as Chögyam Trungpa and Pema Chödrön.
Raniero Gnoli was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Mario Praz and Giuseppe Tucci. He served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Ranu Kunwar is a PhD student attested at the Australian National University in 2026, studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.

Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He held a post at Santa Clara University (attested 2012) and served as professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017).
Raphael Kühner was a linguist who studied at Ernestinum Gotha and the University of Göttingen (~1821–1825). He later taught Georg Bühler.

Raphael von Koeber was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied at the Moscow Conservatory and the universities of Heidelberg and Jena. In 1893, he took up a post at the University of Tokyo.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh was an Indologist and historian who studied at Fergusson College under R. D. Ranade, Dr. Bhune, Sukhlal Sanghvi, and Muni Jinvijaya. He served as professor at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1939) and edited Puratattva (~1922–1926).

Rasmus Rask was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen. He held library and professorial appointments at Copenhagen between 1814 and 1831, teaching Benjamin Thorpe and Adolf Ivar Arwidsson.

Ratna Basu is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1989 and holds a post as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and succeeded him in 2017.
